claims.content: The objective is to transfer reporting responsibility for a reported track to the JU that has the best available positional data, so that only that JU reports the track on the interface; when the transfer is due to a shift in R², the transferring JU ceases reporting the track without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The objective is to transfer reporting responsibility for a reported track to the JU that has the best available positional data, so that only that JU reports the track on the interface; when the transfer is due to a shift in R², the transferring JU ceases reporting the track without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report.

claims.content: C2 JU
A C2 JU currently holds reporting responsibility (R²) for a reported contact/track on the interface, identified by a specific Track Number (TN).
No other JU is currently reporting the same contact using the same Track Number.

Another JU has better/current positional data for the reported item: for a common track, its local track quality (TQ) at the time of transmission exceeds the received TQ by 2 or more; for an emergency point, it has additional or more current information on the point; for a ballistic missile track, its local TQ at or before the time of the remote track time tag exceeds the received TQ by 1 or more.

The JU currently holding reporting responsibility for a real-time track receives a remote track report for that track whose TQ exceeds its local TQ by the applicable threshold — by 2 or more for a common track, or by 1 or more for a ballistic missile track.

For emergency points, the trigger is an operator action by a JU that has additional or more current information on a previously reported point; that JU may report on the point and, as the latest reporter, assumes R².
The C2 JU currently holding R² for the reported real-time track receives a remote track report for that track in which the remote track quality (TQ) is greater than its local TQ.
Because the remote TQ is greater, the C2 JU relinquishes R² for the track to the source JU (the better-positioned JU).
The C2 JU ceases reporting the track; it does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report message, because the cessation is due to a shift in R² to the other JU, not to dropping the track.
The source JU now holds R² and reports the track, so only the JU with the best available positional data reports the track on the interface.

For a previously reported emergency point, any JU may report the point through operator action only when that JU has additional or more current information on the point; the latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.

Diverges from Step 1: For a real-time track, if the remote track report has TQ equal to the local TQ and is from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN, the C2 JU relinquishes R² to that JU.

Diverges from Step 1: When the received Surveillance message or J7.0 (ACT=1) report has an Environment/Category (air, surface/maritime, or land/ground) and ID different from the local Environment/Category and ID, the Environment/Category conflict is processed and resolved before the ID conflict is resolved, and the R² transfer determination continues after that resolution.

Diverges from Step 2: Automatic correlation (and hence automatic R² transfer) is restricted when an ID conflict, a different Mode II code with local code current, both tracks locally derived real-time, or a Strength field greater than 1 exists; for ID conflicts and Mode II code mismatches, the C2 JU may use an initialization parameter/operator-selectable capability to inhibit that restriction, subject to interface coordination and promulgation, and thereby allow the transfer to proceed.

Diverges from Step 2: If the correlated track is one for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers differ, the C2 JU transmits a J7.2 (RV=1) Correlation message with the Source TN from the J2 PPLI Header word as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN, effecting the transfer to the other JU.

Diverges from Step 1: For a reported point, if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another IU may, by operator action only, assume R² for the point using the same Reference TN.
Diverges from Step 1: A JU assumes R² on a common track if its local TQ at the time of transmission exceeds the received TQ by 2 or more.

Diverges from Step 1: If the reported track is a subsurface track, the C2 JU shall not correlate the subsurface track with IUs. Exit: No correlation (and hence no R² transfer) is performed for the subsurface track; the use case terminates without transfer and the C2 JU retains R².

Diverges from Step 1: If the position or other data in the PPLI received from the better-positioned JU meet decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data are decorrelated, and the C2 JU initiates a new surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, reporting both the PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator and IFF/SIF Indicator fields as 'No Statement'. Exit: The R² transfer does not proceed; a new track is reported instead (outside this use case).

Diverges from Step 1: If the PPLI message correlating with the reported track has its Geodetic Position Quality field set to value 0, the C2 JU accepts the J3 surveillance track and discards the PPLI message instead of accepting the PPLI as the better-positioned data. Exit: No transfer is made based on that PPLI; the C2 JU retains R² and the surveillance track.

Diverges from Step 1: If there is a conflict between locally derived information and interface-reported information for the track, the C2 JU resolves the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination. Exit: After the difference is resolved, the transfer determination continues (return to Step 1).

Diverges from Step 1: If the reported track is a ballistic missile track and the recognized difference is in its position or velocity, the C2 JU shall not resolve the difference through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 1 (Difference Report). Exit: The ballistic missile position/velocity difference is not treated as a conflict; the transfer determination continues without a difference report.

Diverges from Step 2: If the track for which R² is being transferred is a ballistic missile track with an associated launch point, the unit assuming R² for the ballistic missile track need not assume R² for the associated launch point, and the unit no longer holding R² on the ballistic missile track may continue to report the launch point in accordance with the transmit/receive rules. Exit: The R² transfer is effected for the ballistic missile track only; the launch point remains reportable by the transferring unit.

Diverges from Step 2: If a correlation request made as part of the R² transfer is rejected, the C2 JU transmits a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Exit: The rejection is reported (J7.2 RV=2) and the transfer based on the rejected correlation does not proceed.

Diverges from Step 2: If the C2 JU receives a J7.2 message containing one or both of the same Track Numbers (TNs) as those contained in the transmission of its own unit's J7.2 message sequence currently in progress, specific exception actions shall be taken. Exit: The specific exception actions for the concurrent same-TN J7.2 condition are executed.

Diverges from Step 3: If the C2 JU ceases reporting the track for a reason other than relinquishing R² to the better-positioned JU (for example, an operator error makes it desirable to change the simulation status of the track), the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report message and a new track shall be reported. Exit: The track is dropped (J7.0 ACT=0) and re-reported; no R² transfer occurs.

Diverges from Step 3: If a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT=0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track, it shall automatically purge those tracks (DRT=0-3) after a specific time interval; under this condition, a J7.0 (ACT=0) message shall not be transmitted. DATUMS (DRT=4) shall not be purged automatically even when no J7.0 (ACT=0) is received and no further updates arrive. Exit: The stale remote track is purged after the specific time interval (DATUMS are excluded from automatic purge).

missing_aspects: Recovery/continuation after the J7.2 same-TN collision exception (EC-EF-029) is not specified in the available evidence; the card only states that 'specific exception actions' are taken.

claims.content: R² for the reported track has been relinquished to the remote JU with superior TQ; that remote JU is now the reporting JU, and the C2 JU has ceased reporting the track, so only the JU with the best available positional data reports the track on the interface.
After the C2 JU ceases reporting the track in this R²-transfer situation, a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report message is not transmitted.
For a reported point, the latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.
For a ballistic missile track, the remote JU assumes R² when its local TQ exceeds the received TQ by 1 or more, becoming the new reporting entity.

For a ballistic missile track with an associated launch point, the unit assuming R² for the ballistic missile track need not assume R² for the launch point; the previous reporter may continue to report the launch point.

quality_flags.detail: [goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal slot's scope_contract (success_boundary and in_scope_actions) says the transferring C2 JU ceases reporting using a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report message, but main_flow Step 3 explicitly states that no J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report is transmitted because the cessation is due to an R² shift, not to dropping the track. This is a goal-conflation issue: the goal scope_contract imports an action from the separate drop-and-re-report use case, so the goal itself needs to be corrected/narrowed rather than the main flow changed. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Specific initiating actor 'C2 JU' is not supported by the cited cards; only a generic JU is supported.; Completion of the transfer by the C2 JU relinquishing R² to the better-positioned JU is not supported by the cited cards.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 7 (EC-EF-029) says that when a J7.2 message contains one or both of the same TNs as an in-progress J7.2 sequence, 'specific exception actions shall be taken', and its exit merely repeats that the specific exception actions are executed. This does not state a concrete outcome: no return to a main_flow step, no explicit termination/failure state, and no handoff, so the branch lacks clear exit coverage. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit recovery/exit evidence is not supported by cited cards: 'handled without unintended loss of R²' and 'the transfer based on the rejected correlation does not proceed'.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] The J7.2 same-TN collision exception says 'specific exception actions shall be taken' and exits with 'specific exception actions ... are executed', but it does not specify whether the branch returns to a main_flow step, terminates, or reaches a concrete failure/prevention state. This is an unspecified outcome rather than a clear exit. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit recovery/exit evidence for the concurrent same-TN J7.2 condition (i.e., that the condition is resolved) is not provided by cited cards.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The emergency-point trigger requires a previously reported emergency point to already have reporting responsibility (R²) before another JU acts, but Precondition 1 only establishes R² for a reported contact/track identified by a Track Number. It does not cover a reported emergency point, so the vertical flow into the emergency-point branch (Trigger claim 2, Main Flow step 5, Postcondition 3) lacks the necessary prior-state guarantee.

[goal_mainflow_alignment] Main Flow Step 5 (claim index 4) introduces a separate reporting-responsibility rule for previously reported emergency points: any JU may report the point by operator action when it has additional/more current information, and the latest JU to report has R². The Goal is limited to transferring reporting responsibility for a reported track to the JU with the best positional data based on TQ and says nothing about operator-initiated point reporting. The Main Flow therefore contains behavior outside the stated Goal, so the Goal is not consistent with the complete Main Flow behavior.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim index 7 (EC-EF-029) lacks a clear exit outcome. It only states that 'specific exception actions' are taken for the concurrent same-TN J7.2 condition, and the exit repeats that those actions are executed. It does not specify whether the transfer is prevented, terminated, retried, or handed off, nor does it define an explicit terminal failure/prevention state.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim index 4 has an incorrect/inconsistent divergence point: its text says 'Diverges from Step 1', but the branch is about a reported point receiving no periodic update for three intervals and another IU assuming R² by operator action. That branch is logically tied to Main Flow Step 5 (point reporting responsibility), and the structured step_number is 5, so the textual divergence reference should say Step 5, not Step 1.

inconsistency_hints: Preconditions define the better-positioned JU only for a common track (TQ exceeds by 2 or more) and for an emergency point (additional/current info). They omit the ballistic-missile threshold that the postconditions rely on: for a BM track, the remote JU assumes R² when its local TQ exceeds the received TQ by 1 or more. Since the trigger and main flow use the generic condition 'remote TQ greater', the BM transfer path is not supported by the required preconditions and the vertical chain to postconditions EC-PO-004/EC-PO-005 is broken.

The main flow only describes the real-time track/TQ handover path. It has no branch for the emergency-point situation already present in preconditions and postcondition EC-PO-000 ('For a reported point, the latest JU to report the point has R²'). Therefore the point postcondition cannot be reached from the main flow.

The goal's success_boundary and in_scope_actions list 'J7.0 (ACT=0)' as the mechanism for ceasing reporting after an R² transfer, but main_flow Step 3 explicitly states that the C2 JU does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Report when the cessation is due to an R² shift. This conflates the R²-transfer use case with the separate drop-track action and must be corrected.

Preconditions define 'better/current positional data' with specific TQ thresholds (common track +2; ballistic missile +1), but the Trigger only says TQ is greater. A +1 common-track report would satisfy the Trigger yet violate Precondition EC-PC-002, so the Trigger can initiate the use case in a state the Preconditions do not cover.

Main Flow step 5 introduces the emergency-point rule (operator action by a JU with additional/current information; latest reporter holds R²), which is not initiated by the Trigger's remote-track-report-with-higher-TQ event. This is a restart of a different scenario rather than a continuation of the Trigger.
